summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 8% YoY to INR686 crore on value growth, with volumes down 6-7% and PAT at INR56.17 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR686 crore, up 8% YoY from INR637 crore, driven by premium mix and price rather than volume. Management said volumes fell about 6-7% due to weak rains and El Nino, with value growth of 4-5%. Gross margin was 33.7% (vs 34.5%), EBITDA INR92.44 crore (13.5% margin) and PAT INR56.17 crore. H1 revenue declined about 2% YoY, with H1 EBITDA at INR161 crore (12.3% margin) and PAT near INR100 crore. Working capital days rose to 158 from 151, and management guided to a volume decline for the full year with H2 improvement in value.

financial_highlights.change: vs 31.7% in H1 FY26, about +100 bps

segments.name: Brand / Kaeros
segments.commentary: Kaeros gross brand turnover about INR75 crore in H1; total Kaeros sales about INR114 crore in H1. Target is brand turnover above INR125 crore this fiscal, with standalone Kaeros around INR200 crore and a doubling planned next year.

segments.name: Maharatna / Focused Maharatna / Gold
segments.commentary: Premium Maharatna and Focused Maharatna products are now above 60% of B2C mix, with a target of 70%. Gold products fell as farmers shifted to new-generation products; management said they are not pushed.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Exports are about 5% of revenue, mainly white-label formulations in more than 25 countries. Technical exports are starting, with more than 10 technicals registered and about 15 AIs in work. Long-term target is INR500 crore by five years out.

segments.name: B2B technicals
segments.commentary: B2B sales are above INR400 crore. Domestic portfolio has 28 technicals.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth not expected this fiscal; value growth expected, with H2 improvement from premium mix and pass-through of raw material costs.
Gross margin expected to hold around 33% this year; management aims to match best-in-industry over time, with a typical gain of about 1% a year.
Q3 and Q4 returns expected to be normal; H1 PAT loss not expected to be fully recovered, but H2 expected positive.
Dahej project to be fully capitalised by December 2026 (Q3). Sotanala formulation start targeted April 2027, possibly May; technical manufacturing and full formulation unit next fiscal.
Only 1-2 launches expected this fiscal, with 3-5 launches next fiscal. OAT Agrio product launch likely slips by a few months to next fiscal.
Post Sotanala completion, major capex cycle ends and interest costs normalise, with positive cash flow expected.
capex_capacity: Dahej plant partially in production and partially capitalised; full capitalisation expected in Q3 FY27 after a December shutdown and restart, with utility and electricity gaps fixed.
Sotanala: formulation start targeted April 2027 (possible 1-2 month slip due to NCR gas supply), technical manufacturing and complete formulation unit in FY28.
Planned state-of-the-art DCS plant for CDMO, plus Dahej upgrade for CDMO work at both sites.
Four R&D centres, including Chopanki and Dahej (both NABL), plus a discovery centre in a JV with a Japanese company (Japanese partner funds 80%).
demand_pricing: Volume fell about 6-7% in Q2, with value up 4-5%, as the company sold more premium products; weak rains hit herbicides and granules.
Inflation is visible in agri commodity prices; farmers are moving to premium products and fewer sprays, and farmer profitability is largely intact despite low yields.
Field activity in H1: more than 18,000 farmer meetings, more than 9,000 demonstrations and more than 2.5 lakh farmers met. Around 70 ICS crop-solution plots this year, up from about 30.
Third-party field team ranges from 750 to 1,300-1,400 by season; H2 expected near 750. Kaeros adds about 150 people (70-80 on roll).
Crude oil spiked to about $125 and freight costs rose, pressuring the business; management said the impact is still to be seen in the festive season.
Channel returns were high but lower than last year. Most returns were taken in Q2; Q3 expected to be normal. Secondary visibility is partial (DMS and QR coverage of 15-20%).

qa_highlights.question: What was the volume growth by B2B, B2C and export, and how did Maharatna products perform?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume was negative, down about 6-7%; value grew 4-5%. Gold products fell while Focused Maharatna and Maharatna grew, with Maharatna showing a decent rise in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Will volumes decline for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said this is not a volume-growth year, but value growth is expected, with H2 improvements from a mix of premium products and price pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kaeros outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Kaeros brand turnover is about INR75 crore in H1. The target is above INR125 crore this year, with standalone Kaeros around INR200 crore and a planned doubling next year. The national network is to be complete in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the OAT Agrio launch and the 9(3) registrations?
qa_highlights.answer: No immediate launch this calendar year. The schedule inclusion application is pending CIB inquiry, so the launch could slip a few months. Nissan's new product is due in kharif, followed by 9(3) mixtures.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export strategy and cost competitiveness versus China?
qa_highlights.answer: Shifting from white-label brand exports to technicals, with more than 10 registrations and about 15 AIs in work. CDMO deals are early-stage, mostly with Japanese players. Exports are about 5% of revenue, with a target of INR500 crore in five years.

qa_highlights.question: How much R&D is spent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the R&D expense shown is about INR12 crore, with some trial costs booked under marketing. More than 100 registrations are involved, with about 200 people across IIL and the OIL JV.

risks_watch: Volume decline of 6-7% in Q2 and full-year volume decline; dependence on value growth and price pass-through.
Working capital stretched: inventory INR814 crore and debtors INR719 crore, with NWC near INR1,000 crore; cash flow improvement not yet visible.
Dahej full capitalisation slipped from H1 to Q3; Sotanala timeline could slip further.
Regulatory timing for OAT Agrio and 9(3) products; registrations and schedule inclusion are pending.
Partial secondary-sales visibility (DMS and QR coverage 15-20%) and channel returns.
Crude and freight volatility, El Nino effects, and Kaeros scaling to the targeted INR125 crore brand turnover.
summary.management_tone: Confident on premiumisation, Kaeros and CDMO, but cautious on volume and H1 earnings, with management conceding that recovery of the H1 loss is not visible. Several timelines (Dahej, Sotanala, OAT) were pushed back or qualified during the call.
key_quotes: So the volume growth will be down this year. I'll not be able to make it, but I'm very, very sure that there will be value growth, and we'll be able to make some improvements in H2 of this year.
Premiumization and Kaeros expansion will support profitable growth for IIL.
There are more than 55 products which have already hit the market, and there will be a few more.
So the target is to cross INR125 crores of brand turnover in Kaeros.

adds.what: Dahej plant full capitalisation (partly in production; utility and electricity gaps being fixed)
Sotanala formulation unit (start targeted April 2027, possibly May; technical manufacturing and full formulation in FY28)

growth.why: Management guides volume decline for FY27 with value growth and H2 improvement from premium mix and raw-material pass-through, gross margin around 33%, and H1 revenue down about 2%; Dahej full capitalisation is due Q3 and Sotanala formulation April 2027, but no revenue growth number is guided and volumes are falling 6-7%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin guided around 33% for FY27 vs 33.7% in Q2 and 34.5% a year ago, with H1 gross margin up about 100 bps to 32.7%; management targets ~1% a year gain but crude spike and freight pressure are still to show in festive season.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Dahej plant is partly in production and full capitalisation is guided for December 2026 (Q3) after a shutdown; Sotanala formulation start targeted April 2027 (possible 1-2 month slip), so new capacity comes live within the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volumes fell 6-7% in Q2 and management said full-year volume will decline, with growth coming only from value and premium mix.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says the major capex cycle ends after Sotanala and interest costs normalise, with cash flow expected positive; utilisation is not discussed as a constraint (no 80%+ utilisation read), though a planned DCS plant for CDMO and Dahej CDMO upgrade are already on the list.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue down about 2%, H1 PAT loss not expected to be fully recovered, and volume guided down; only H2 value improvement is expected, so a raise is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Crude at about $125 and rising freight costs are still to hit in the festive season, OAT Agrio may slip a few months, Sotanala may slip 1-2 months on NCR gas supply, and working capital days rose to 158 from 151.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Only 1-2 launches expected this fiscal with 3-5 next fiscal; Nissan's new product is due in kharif and OAT Agrio may slip a few months into next fiscal.

rows.label: Premium mix shift to Maharatna / Focused Maharatna
rows.why: Premium Maharatna and Focused Maharatna are above 60% of B2C mix with a 70% target, and management expects H2 value improvement from premium mix and raw-material pass-through despite 6-7% volume decline.

rows.label: Technical exports and CDMO ramp
rows.why: Exports are about 5% of revenue with more than 10 technicals registered and about 15 AIs in work; INR500 crore target in five years (40-50% CAGR) but CDMO deals are early-stage.

rows.label: Working capital release
rows.why: Working capital days rose to 158 from 151 and NWC is about INR1,000 crore vs INR966 crore a year earlier, with inventory INR814 crore and debtors INR719 crore; cash flow improvement not yet visible.

tone.note: Management was confident on premiumisation, Kaeros and CDMO, but cautious on volumes, H1 earnings and timelines, with Dahej and OAT Agrio pushed back; analysts probed volume trends, Maharatna mix and the Kaeros and export targets.
